name: Publish the annual report and results
summary: Each year the model manager must give the Minister of Finance an annual report with audited financial statements within 120 days of year end, and publishes it with a results release in April. Corporate communications plans the report in the autumn, interviews leaders and drafts the narrative, while finance, performance, responsible investing, governance and HR write their sections once results, audited statements and pay decisions are final. The full draft is fact-checked, reviewed by legal and the executive, designed, read by the auditor, approved by the board and made accessible before publication. The fixed late-February audit date, many contributors and late changes after design make the last six weeks tight and error-prone.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with a four-person corporate communications team and an outside design agency.
baseline.notes: Word drafts in a shared document folder, spreadsheet tie-out logs, an agency-designed PDF with an accessible version, board approval through the board portal.

trigger: The annual planning cycle starts in the autumn; year-end performance results, the stewardship report and the audited financial statements feed the report as they become final.
end_state: The annual report has been approved by the board, submitted to the Minister of Finance, published on the website and sent to clients, and the results release has been issued.

volume.seasonality: One report a year, published in April.

evidence.note: One annual report a year required by the manager's governing act and published every year since 2017.

steps.name: Plan the report and its timetable
steps.description: In the autumn the vice president of communications drafts the theme, page plan, section owners and timetable back from the April release, reviews last year's lessons and books design and print capacity, and presents the plan to the executive team.

evidence.note: Run the report as a project with an executive sponsor, section owners and a timetable; times tier C.

steps.name: Chief executive approves the theme and key messages
steps.description: The chief executive reviews the proposed theme, key messages, page plan and timetable with the executive team and approves them or asks for changes in emphasis.

evidence.note: Key themes and messages set at the start and signed off by the sponsor; times tier C.

steps.name: Brief the design agency
steps.description: A communications advisor briefs the design agency on the theme, page count, charts, photography and accessible PDF requirements, agrees the quote and production schedule under the procurement rules and sets proof dates.

evidence.note: Blueprint for layout, graphics and imagery agreed early; times tier C.

steps.name: Send content requests to section owners
steps.description: The advisor sends each section owner (investment departments, risk, finance, human resources, governance, responsible investing) a template, word count, style guide, list of figures needed and deadlines, and sets up the shared folder for drafts and backup.

evidence.note: Writing-style guidance and a central store of statistics with backup; times tier C.

steps.name: Interview leaders and draft the narrative sections
steps.description: The advisors interview the chair, CEO, CIO and department heads and draft the chair and CEO reports, investment department pages, operations and people sections, then circulate each draft to its owner for corrections.

error.defect_description: A figure or claim in the narrative is outdated or unsupported.

evidence.note: Narrative can be drafted before the financials are ready (icaew_ar); section list from mgr_ar21. Waits for interview slots over December and January and touch times are tier C.

steps.name: Draft the responsible investing section
steps.description: The head of responsible investing drafts the ESG and stewardship pages: voting and engagement statistics from the stewardship report, climate action plan progress and portfolio climate metrics, and examples from the asset classes.

evidence.note: Responsible investing section and climate action plan reporting; times tier C.

steps.name: Draft the governance section
steps.description: The board secretariat drafts the governance pages: board composition and appointments, committee mandates and work, attendance, director biographies and director remuneration, and confirms them with the chair of the governance committee.

evidence.note: Corporate governance section with committees and board biographies; times tier C.

steps.name: Draft wait for year-end results and audited statements
steps.description: The draft report waits while the year is closed: performance results by client, pool and asset class are approved in February and the board authorises the audited financial statements in late February or early March.

evidence.note: Financial statements authorised on 25 February 2021, 24 February 2022 and 2 March 2023; the wait length depends on when drafting finished and is tier C.

steps.name: Draft the financial and cost sections
steps.description: The manager of financial reporting drafts the management's discussion and analysis on costs, cost recovery and financial position, inserts the audited financial statements and notes, and lists the backup for every figure.

error.defect_description: Cost figure in the narrative differs from the audited statements.

evidence.note: Cost management and financial statements sections; times tier C.

steps.name: Supply and verify the performance figures
steps.description: The manager of performance provides the approved weighted average client return, client range, benchmark and value added, asset class results and multi-year returns, and checks the charts the writers built from them.

error.defect_description: Wrong period or benchmark in a return table.

evidence.note: The report and release quote weighted average and range of client returns and asset class results; times tier C.

steps.name: Draft the compensation discussion and analysis
steps.description: The total rewards manager drafts the compensation discussion and analysis and executive pay tables once incentive awards are approved, and the head of HR takes it to the Human Resources and Compensation Committee chair for review.

control.basis: Board Human Resources and Compensation Committee review of compensation disclosure

evidence.note: Compensation discussion and analysis section and committee report; times tier C.

steps.name: Chief financial officer reviews the financial content
steps.description: The chief financial officer reviews the financial and cost sections, the performance tables and the way results are described, and returns comments or approves them.

evidence.note: CFO review of financial content is common practice; rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Assemble and edit the full draft
steps.description: The vice president of communications combines all sections, edits for a consistent voice and balanced messages, removes repetition, checks the theme carries through and sends the complete draft for fact checking.

evidence.note: Many authors produce a disjointed document; review the full report for consistency; times tier C.

steps.name: Fact-check and tie out every number
steps.description: An advisor checks every figure, date and claim in the draft against the audited statements, approved performance results, transaction lists and the backup folder, logs mismatches and gets owners to correct them.

control.basis: Disclosure practice: every published figure traced to approved source schedules

evidence.note: Tie-out of reported numbers to audited figures; late changes make errors almost inevitable. Rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Legal review of the disclosures
steps.description: The general counsel reviews the draft for confidential deal or client information, forward-looking statements, compensation disclosure and statements about clients, the Minister and regulators, and marks required changes.

evidence.note: Legal review of public disclosure is common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Executive review of the full draft
steps.description: The chief executive, with the CIO and executive team, reads the full draft and approves it for design or asks for changes to messages, emphasis or the treatment of the year's results.

evidence.note: Executive sign-off is common practice; rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Design agency lays out the proof
steps.description: The design agency flows the approved text, charts and photographs into the layout and returns a proof, or a revised proof after the last round of corrections.

evidence.note: Agency proof turnaround of three to ten days is tier C.

steps.name: Proofread the designed report
steps.description: Advisors and a reviewer not involved in drafting check the proof for typography, page numbers, cross-references, chart labels and figures that moved in layout, and send consolidated corrections to the agency.

error.defect_description: Layout change breaks a figure or cross-reference.

evidence.note: Cold reviews of grammar, page numbers, headings and cross-references; rounds tier C.

steps.name: External auditor reads the report for consistency
steps.description: The external auditor reads the designed report alongside the audited financial statements and confirms that the other information is consistent with them, raising any material inconsistency before release.

control.basis: Canadian Auditing Standard 720: auditor's responsibilities for other information

evidence.note: Auditors read other information in documents containing audited statements under Canadian Auditing Standard 720, not opened here; times tier C.

steps.name: Board approves the annual report
steps.description: The board, usually on the recommendation of the Finance and Audit Committee, approves the annual report for submission to the Minister and publication, at a scheduled meeting or by written resolution.

control.basis: The model manager Act, 2015, section 23: Board submits the annual report

evidence.note: Section 23 of the manager's governing act requires the Board to submit the annual report; meeting timing is tier C.

steps.name: Make the final PDF accessible
steps.description: The agency or an accessibility specialist tags the final PDF for reading order, headings and tables, adds alternative text to charts and images and checks contrast; the advisor tests it with a checker and screen reader before release.

control.basis: Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, Integrated Accessibility Standards: web content to WCAG 2.0 Level AA

evidence.note: WCAG 2.0 Level AA text alternatives and contrast; the model manager's report files carry an accessible-version marker in their names. Ontario's accessibility standard for web content was not opened, times tier C.

steps.name: Draft the results release and media materials
steps.description: The vice president of communications drafts the results news release, key messages and questions and answers for media and stakeholders, aligned with the report's figures, and plans the release date and distribution.

evidence.note: Results releases on 13 April 2021, 25 April 2022 and 13 April 2023 quote the report's figures; times tier C.

steps.name: Chief executive approves the release
steps.description: The chief executive and chief financial officer approve the release wording and figures and the spokesperson messages, after the CFO checks every number against the report.

control.basis: Disclosure policy: CEO approval of public results releases

evidence.note: Executive approval of releases is common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Submit the report to the Minister of Finance
steps.description: The board secretariat prepares the chair's covering letter and delivers the annual report with the audited financial statements to the Minister of Finance before the 120-day deadline, and confirms receipt with the ministry.

control.basis: The model manager Act, 2015, section 23: annual report to the Minister within 120 days of year end

evidence.note: Annual report with audited statements to the Minister within 120 days after year end.

steps.name: Publish the report and issue the release
steps.description: On release day the advisor posts the report on the website, issues the news release through the wire service, sends the report to clients and stakeholders, posts on social media and hands media enquiries to the spokespeople.

evidence.note: Releases link to the report on the website; annual reports have been published every year since 2017.

exceptions.name: Financial content rework
exceptions.description: The CFO sends the financial and cost sections back for changes before the full draft is assembled.

exceptions.name: Messages changed at executive review
exceptions.description: The executive asks for changes to messages or the treatment of the year's results, sending the draft back through editing, fact checking and legal review.

exceptions.name: Extra proof rounds
exceptions.description: Late text or figure changes need another designed proof.

exceptions.name: Auditor or board finds an inconsistency
exceptions.description: The auditor's reading or the board raises a point that must be corrected in the proof.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from planning kick-off to publication

evidence.note: Publication on 13 April 2021, 25 April 2022 and 13 April 2023, inside the 120-day limit after 31 December; a mid-November kick-off is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Most financial content cannot be finished until the audited statements are authorised in late February, leaving about six weeks for financial drafting, review, design, auditor reading, board approval and accessibility work.

evidence.note: Statements authorised 24 February 2022 and release on 25 April 2022.

pain_points.description: Many contributors write in different styles and late changes ripple through text, charts and the designed proof, so figures are re-checked several times.
Review by CFO, legal, CEO, auditor and board happens one after another, each waiting for availability.

evidence.note: Author's reading of common practice.

sources.supports: Annual reports listed for every year from 2017 to 2025.

sources.title: Overcoming the challenges faced when preparing the annual report (By All Accounts, January 2022)
sources.supports: Run the report as a project with an executive sponsor, project manager and section owners tracked to a timetable; draft narrative early, before financials; many authors make the report disjointed; numerous versions and late changes make errors almost inevitable, so keep a central store of statistics and backup shared with auditors; cold reviews of grammar, page numbers and cross-references; check printer proofs.

sources.title: Financial statement tie-out
sources.supports: Tie-out confirms that reported numbers agree with the audited figures and reconciles differences; steps are gathering data, comparing line items, investigating mismatches, correcting errors and sign-off; transposed numbers are a typical error; the work is time-intensive.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0
sources.supports: W3C Recommendation of 11 December 2008; Level AA requires all Level A and AA success criteria, including text alternatives for non-text content (1.1.1) and a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text (1.4.3).

assumptions: The case runs from the autumn kick-off to publication; the upstream objects (financial statements, performance results, stewardship report) arrive during the case, so the trigger shares describe which input most often sets the pace rather than separate cases.

From the 2022 report onward the model manager also published a separate climate action plan; a separate responsible investing report is mentioned in the organisation file but not modelled here, where the responsible investing section is drafted inside the annual report.

Section drafting by finance, performance and HR after year end runs in parallel and is marked concurrent; the simulator adds those hands-on hours in sequence, which overstates elapsed time by a few days.
The board (an external party in the organisation file) approves the report; its members' time is not costed. The external auditor's reading is shown as a wait; its fee sits in the audit process.
The auditor's reading of other information (Canadian Auditing Standard 720) and Ontario's accessibility standard are named from general knowledge because their texts could not be opened.
Design agency, printing and wire service fees are external costs not modelled as labour.

mgr_financial_reporting, mgr_performance, hr_rewards_manager, board_secretary and general_counsel are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process; they write or review sections.

Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, variable pay and a 1.35 loading). Hands-on time of about 330 hours across in-house roles is the author's estimate.
Web searching ran out while this workflow was researched, so sources were limited to pages fetched by address and saved copies of the model manager's annual reports.
